svg.text: First aid: the do-nots are what the examiner asks about
BURNS
Cool with clean running water for 20 MINUTES
Remove jewellery and clothing unless stuck
Cover with clean non-fluffy material or cling film
Do NOT apply ice, toothpaste, egg, palm oil,
shea butter or herbal preparations.
SNAKEBITE
Keep the person still and calm. Immobilise the
limb at heart level. Transport urgently.
Do NOT cut the wound, suck the venom,
apply a tight tourniquet, use ice, or give
alcohol. Movement pumps venom onward.
EPISTAXIS — nose bleed
Sit UP and lean FORWARD
Pinch the SOFT part of the nose for 10 minutes
without releasing to check
Do NOT tilt the head back — blood then runs
down the throat, is swallowed, and causes
SEIZURE
Protect the head, clear the area, time it,
recovery position AFTER it stops
Do NOT restrain the person and do NOT put
anything in the mouth. They cannot swallow
the tongue. You will break teeth or fingers.
Call for help if it lasts over 5 minutes.
SEVERE BLEEDING
DIRECT PRESSURE on the wound, firmly
Elevate the limb if no fracture
Add dressings ON TOP — do not remove soaked
ones, you strip away the forming clot
Tourniquet only for catastrophic limb bleeding
that pressure cannot control. Note the TIME.
An embedded object is left in place and padded around.
FRACTURE and SPINAL INJURY
Immobilise the joint ABOVE and BELOW
Check circulation beyond the splint before
and after applying it
Suspected spine: do NOT move unless there is
danger. Manual in-line stabilisation of the head.
If they must be moved, log roll with enough
people to keep head, spine and pelvis aligned.
